Documentation Overview

This page provides access to the official public documentation of the Voltorus gravitational energy research program.

The page contains official public resources for VOLTORUS technologies focused on energy systems, energy markets, and regulatory compliance. This includes technical guides, APIs, integration docs, and system diagrams.

  • 🧩 APIs & Integrations – Technical references and guides for integrating with VOLTORUS platforms and services.
  • 📚 Use cases, technical whitepapers, and system diagrams to support implementation and research.

Industrial Processes Powered by Gravitational Energy Systems

This section presents the industrial applications that can be potentially supplied by a continuous electrical power source generated by the gravitational energy system.


  • Containerized Green Electricity Generation
    • Continuous off-grid electrical power production.
    • Replacement of diesel generators for remote installations.
    • Power supply for industrial equipment and critical infrastructure.
    • Baseload electricity for manufacturing facilities and microgrids.

  • Atmospheric Water Generation (AWG)
    • Electrical power for atmospheric water generators.
    • Production of potable water from ambient humidity.
    • Water supply for remote communities, agriculture and industrial processes.
    • Fully autonomous containerized water production.

  • Green Hydrogen Production
    • Electrolysis powered by continuous electrical energy.
    • Hydrogen production using purified water.
    • Oxygen recovery as an industrial by-product.
    • Hydrogen supply for mobility, chemical industries and energy storage.

  • Direct Air Carbon Capture (DAC)
    • Continuous electrical supply for CO₂ capture systems.
    • Atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration.
    • Carbon feedstock for synthetic fuel production.
    • Support for carbon management strategies.

  • Synthetic Fuel Production
    • Sabatier reactors producing renewable methane (e-methane).
    • Fischer–Tropsch synthesis producing e-crude, e-diesel and e-methanol.
    • Integration of green hydrogen and captured CO₂.
    • Production of renewable fuels for maritime, aviation and heavy industry.

  • Industrial Heat & Process Energy
    • Electrical heating systems.
    • Steam generation through electric boilers.
    • Heat pumps for industrial thermal processes.
    • Support for food processing and chemical manufacturing.

  • Water Treatment & Desalination
    • Reverse osmosis desalination plants.
    • Industrial wastewater treatment.
    • Ultrafiltration and purification systems.
    • Municipal drinking water production.

  • Data Centers & Digital Infrastructure
    • Continuous power supply for servers.
    • Edge computing facilities.
    • Telecommunication infrastructure.
    • AI computing clusters and cloud platforms.

  • Manufacturing & Industrial Automation
    • CNC machining centers.
    • Robotic production lines.
    • Industrial automation equipment.
    • Packaging and logistics systems.

  • Mining & Remote Industrial Sites
    • Autonomous electrical supply for mining operations.
    • Power for drilling, crushing and material handling.
    • Energy independence in isolated locations.
    • Reduction of diesel fuel logistics.

  • Agriculture & Food Production
    • Irrigation pumping systems.
    • Controlled-environment agriculture.
    • Cold storage and refrigeration.
    • Livestock and aquaculture facilities.

  • Smart Grid & Microgrid Integration
    • Containerized autonomous microgrids.
    • Industrial energy hubs.
    • Backup and resilient electrical infrastructure.
    • Hybrid integration with solar, wind and battery systems.

Industrial Perspective:
A continuous electrical power source can support a wide range of industrial processes, including electricity generation, water production, hydrogen production, carbon capture, synthetic fuel synthesis, manufacturing, digital infrastructure and autonomous microgrids.
The suitability of any specific application depends on the demonstrated performance, reliability, safety and regulatory compliance of the underlying power generation technology.

International electricity generation without license

Electricity generation regulations

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Algeria and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial, agricultural or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Algerian electricity generation is regulated under Law No. 02-01 of 5 February 2002 relating to electricity and public gas distribution, together with its implementing regulations.

The Commission de Régulation de l'Électricité et du Gaz (CREG) distinguishes electricity-generation installations according to their purpose, installed capacity and connection to the electricity network.

For self-consumption installations, the principal threshold identified by the CREG is 25 MW under ISO conditions. Installations below this threshold are subject to a declaration regime, while installations at or above 25 MW require an operating authorization.

Operating Mode Completely off-grid / isolated / island operation
Public Grid Connection None intended
Electricity Import No
Electricity Export No

National Electricity Framework Law No. 02-01 of 5 February 2002 relating to electricity and public gas distribution
Regulator Commission de Régulation de l'Électricité et du Gaz (CREG)
Self-consumption declaration threshold Installed capacity below 25 MW under ISO conditions
Operating authorization threshold 25 MW or more
Administrative Requirements

An isolated self-consumption installation is not automatically free from all administrative requirements.

Under the Algerian electricity framework, an electricity-generation installation intended for self-consumption with installed capacity below 25 MW under ISO conditions is subject to a prior declaration rather than the operating-authorization regime.

Self-consumption below 25 MW

The CREG identifies installations intended for self-consumption with installed capacity below 25 MW under ISO conditions as being subject to the declaration regime.

The declaration is made to the electricity and gas regulatory authority and must comply with the applicable technical and legal requirements.

Therefore, the absence of a grid connection does not eliminate the requirement to declare an installation falling within this regime.

Installations at or above 25 MW

Self-consumption installations with installed capacity of 25 MW or more are subject to the operating-authorization regime.

The CREG evaluates authorization applications according to criteria including safety, energy efficiency, primary energy source, site selection, land use, environmental protection and the technical and financial capabilities of the applicant.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Prior declaration to the CREG where applicable.
  • Operating authorization where the applicable capacity threshold is reached.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Construction and structural requirements.
  • Land-use requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Technical requirements applicable to the particular generation technology.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • No physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity import.
  • No electricity export.
  • No electricity sale to third parties.
  • No electricity purchase from the public network.
  • Electricity used exclusively for internal self-consumption.
  • Independent island operation.
  • Electrical protection preventing accidental energisation of the public network.
  • Prior declaration to the CREG where required.
  • Compliance with environmental, construction, electrical and safety requirements.
Maximum Electrical Power
Maximum capacity below the operating-authorization threshold:

Less than 25 MW

Self-consumption installations below 25 MW under ISO conditions fall under the declaration regime. At 25 MW or above, an operating authorization is required.

The relevant legal threshold for an isolated self-consumption installation is therefore 25 MW .

The legally precise formulation is "less than 25 MW" for the declaration regime.

A 25 MW installation should not be classified as being below the authorization threshold.

References
  1. Law No. 02-01 of 5 February 2002 relating to electricity and public gas distribution.
  2. Executive Decree No. 06-428 of 26 November 2006 concerning the procedure for granting operating authorizations for electricity-generation installations.
  3. Ministerial Order of 2 April 2007 establishing the declaration procedure for electricity production installations.
  4. Commission de Régulation de l'Électricité et du Gaz (CREG) — electricity production and authorization/declaration procedures.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The 25 MW figure is the regulatory threshold identified by the Algerian electricity regulator for distinguishing the declaration regime from the operating-authorization regime for self-consumption electricity-generation installations. It is not a technology-specific mechanical or engineering limit for gravity-powered generation. The proposed installation must also comply with applicable construction, environmental, electrical-safety, land-use and technical requirements.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Angola and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial, agricultural or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Angolan electricity generation is governed by the Lei Geral de Electricidade and its implementing regulations.

Presidential Decree No. 76/21 of 25 March 2021 regulates electricity production, transmission, distribution and commercialization.

The regulation expressly distinguishes self-production from public electricity production. Self-production for own use is a free activity subject to the applicable regulatory and technical rules.

Self-production threshold without establishment/exploitation licence Up to 100 kVA
Licensing threshold Above 100 kVA
Administrative Requirements

Angola expressly recognizes electricity production for own use as auto-production.

Presidential Decree No. 76/21 establishes a specific treatment for self-production installations with installed capacity up to 100 kVA.

Self-production up to 100 kVA

Self-production systems with installed capacity up to 100 kVA do not require an establishment or exploitation licence under Article 45(2) of Presidential Decree No. 76/21.

Instead, registration of a term of responsibility is sufficient, subject to the applicable regulatory requirements.

This is the principal capacity threshold relevant to a small isolated self-consumption installation.

Self-production above 100 kVA

Self-producers with installed capacity above 100 kVA must license their generating centres under the applicable electricity-generation licensing regulations.

The absence of a public-grid connection does not remove this capacity-based licensing requirement.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Registration of the term of responsibility for systems up to 100 kVA.
  • Establishment and exploitation licensing above 100 kVA.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Construction requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Structural and mechanical safety requirements.
  • Technical requirements specific to the generation technology.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • No physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity import.
  • No electricity export.
  • No electricity sale to third parties.
  • Electricity used exclusively for internal self-consumption.
  • Maintain the installation at or below 100 kVA if the project is intended to remain within the non-licensed self-production category.
  • Register the required term of responsibility.
  • Install appropriate electrical protection.
  • Comply with applicable construction, environmental and safety requirements.
Maximum Electrical Power
Maximum self-production capacity without establishment/exploitation licence:

100 kVA

Self-production systems with installed capacity up to 100 kVA do not require an establishment or exploitation licence under Article 45(2) of Presidential Decree No. 76/21.

The exact legal threshold identified for the non-licensed self-production category is 100 kVA.

Above 100 kVA, the generating centre must be licensed under the applicable electricity-generation licensing framework.

References
  1. Lei Geral de Electricidade — Lei No. 14-A/96 of 31 May 1996, as amended.
  2. Presidential Decree No. 76/21 of 25 March 2021.
  3. Article 13 — electricity production and self-production.
  4. Article 16 — licensing of electricity-generation installations.
  5. Article 45 — electricity production outside the Public Electricity System and self-production.
  6. IRSEA — Instituto Regulador dos Serviços de Electricidade e Águas.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The 100 kVA figure is the capacity threshold established by Presidential Decree No. 76/21 for self-production systems that do not require an establishment or exploitation licence. It is not a technology-specific mechanical limit for gravity-powered generation. The proposed installation must also comply with applicable electrical, construction, environmental, structural and safety requirements.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Benin and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial, agricultural, commercial or service requirements under the control of the producer.

Electricity generation and self-production are regulated under the Electricity Code of the Republic of Benin and its implementing regulations.

Decree No. 2021-596 of 12 November 2021 establishes the declaration and authorization procedures applicable to electricity self-production installations.

The current regulatory framework distinguishes self-production installations according to installed capacity, with declaration and authorization regimes applying above defined thresholds.

Administrative Requirements

Benin has established a specific regulatory framework for electricity self-production.

Self-production up to 50 kVA

The current capacity-based framework begins the declaration regime above 50 kVA.

Accordingly, installations with capacity up to and including 50 kVA fall below the declaration threshold established for self-production.

Self-production from above 50 to below 500 kVA

Self-production installations with capacity above 50 kVA and below 500 kVA are subject to the declaration regime.

The declaration must be made to the Autorité de Régulation de l'Électricité before the installation is placed into service.

Self-production above 500 kVA

Self-production installations with capacity above 500 kVA require an authorization.

The authorization procedure includes technical and safety information concerning the proposed installation.

Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • No physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity import.
  • No electricity export.
  • No electricity sale to third parties.
  • Electricity used exclusively for internal self-consumption.
  • Keep the installation at or below 50 kVA if the objective is to remain below the declaration threshold.
  • Install appropriate electrical protection.
  • Comply with applicable construction, environmental and safety requirements.
Maximum Electrical Power
Maximum self-production capacity below the declaration threshold:

50 kVA

The declaration regime begins above 50 kVA. Authorization is required above 500 kVA.

For a completely isolated self-consumption facility, the relevant capacity threshold below which the declaration regime does not apply is 50 kVA.

A facility above 50 kVA enters the declaration regime, while a facility above 500 kVA enters the authorization regime.

References
  1. Law No. 2020-05 of 1 April 2020 establishing the Electricity Code in the Republic of Benin.
  2. Decree No. 2021-596 of 12 November 2021 concerning declaration and authorization procedures for electricity self-production installations.
  3. Autorité de Régulation de l'Électricité (ARE).
  4. Relevant implementing regulations concerning electricity self-production.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The 50 kVA figure is the threshold below which the capacity-based declaration regime for electricity self-production does not apply under the identified regulatory framework. It is not a technology-specific engineering limit for gravity-powered generation. Construction, electrical, environmental, safety and other applicable requirements must also be verified before development.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Botswana and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial, agricultural or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Electricity generation in Botswana is principally regulated under the Electricity Supply Act and the regulatory framework administered by the Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA).

The Electricity Supply Act establishes a general licensing requirement for generation while providing a specific exemption for qualifying small self-generation installations located entirely on the owner's premises where no public electricity supply is available.

Administrative Requirements

Botswana generally requires a licence for electricity generation, supply, transmission, distribution, export or import.

A specific exemption applies to qualifying self-generation installations located entirely on the owner's property and used solely by the owner where no public electricity supply is available.

Owner-premises self-generation

The current framework, following the 2007 and 2016 amendments, maintains a capacity threshold of 100 kW for the qualifying self-generation exemption.

The installation must satisfy the conditions attached to the exemption, including its location on the owner's property and its use solely by the owner.

The absence of public electricity supply is an important condition of the statutory exemption.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Electricity-generation licence where the statutory exemption does not apply.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Construction and structural requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Occupational safety requirements.
  • Requirements imposed by BERA.
  • Technical requirements specific to the gravity-generation installation.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • Locate the installation entirely on the owner's property.
  • Use the electricity solely by the owner.
  • Ensure that no public electricity supply is available if relying on the statutory exemption.
  • Keep the qualifying installation at or below 100 kW.
  • No electricity import.
  • No electricity export.
  • No electricity sale to third parties.
  • No public-grid connection.
  • Install appropriate electrical protection.
  • Comply with applicable safety and environmental requirements.
Maximum Electrical Power
Maximum qualifying self-generation capacity:

100 kW

The 100 kW threshold applies to the statutory self-generation exemption where the other conditions of the Electricity Supply Act are satisfied.

The relevant capacity value for the comparative database is therefore 100 kW.

This value is a statutory exemption threshold and not a technology-specific engineering limit for gravity-powered generation.

References
  1. Electricity Supply Act, Chapter 73:01.
  2. Electricity Supply Act amendments of 2007 and 2016.
  3. Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority Act, 2016.
  4. Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA).
  5. Electricity Supply (Licensing) Regulations.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The 100 kW figure is the statutory capacity threshold associated with the qualifying self-generation exemption identified in the Botswana electricity framework. The exemption also depends on conditions concerning the owner's property, exclusive use and availability of public electricity supply. The figure is not a technology-specific engineering limit for gravity-powered generation.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Burkina Faso and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial, agricultural, commercial or institutional electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

The electricity sector of Burkina Faso is regulated under Law No. 053-2012/AN of 17 December 2012 on the general regulation of the electricity subsector.

The law establishes different regimes for electricity production, including specific rules for installations in the second segment of the electricity subsector.

The law expressly excludes electricity-generation installations with capacity of 10 kW or less from the prior authorization regime identified for production in the second segment.

Administrative Requirements

Burkina Faso's electricity legislation distinguishes between the first and second segments of the electricity subsector.

Installations up to 10 kW

Article 49 of Law No. 053-2012/AN provides that electricity-generation installations with capacity less than or equal to 10 kW are excluded from the prior authorization regime applicable to the second segment.

This is the principal statutory threshold relevant to a small isolated self-consumption installation.

Installations above 10 kW

Electricity-generation installations above 10 kW and below 25 kW are subject to the authorization regime identified in Article 49.

The legislation provides for government authorization, with the regulatory authority involved according to the applicable procedures.

The regulatory treatment therefore changes once the installation exceeds 10 kW.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Declaration requirements where applicable.
  • Authorization requirements above the applicable threshold.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Construction requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Structural and mechanical safety requirements.
  • Technical requirements specific to the generation technology.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • No physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity import.
  • No electricity export.
  • No electricity sale to third parties.
  • Electricity used exclusively for internal self-consumption.
  • Keep the installation at or below 10 kW if the objective is to remain below the prior authorization threshold.
  • Install appropriate electrical protection.
  • Comply with applicable construction, environmental and safety requirements.
Maximum Electrical Power
Maximum generation capacity excluded from the prior authorization regime:

10 kW

Article 49 of Law No. 053-2012/AN excludes installations with generation capacity less than or equal to 10 kW from the prior authorization regime specified for the second segment.

The relevant statutory threshold for the comparative database is therefore 10 kW.

Above 10 kW, the regulatory regime changes and authorization requirements may apply.

References
  1. Law No. 053-2012/AN of 17 December 2012 regulating the electricity subsector in Burkina Faso.
  2. Article 48 — organization of the second segment of the electricity subsector.
  3. Article 49 — electricity production and authorization thresholds.
  4. Autorité de Régulation du Sous-secteur de l'Électricité (ARSE).
  5. Applicable implementing decrees concerning licences, authorizations and declarations.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The 10 kW figure is the statutory threshold identified in Article 49 of Law No. 053-2012/AN for exclusion from the prior authorization regime applicable to electricity production in the second segment. It is not a technology-specific engineering limit for gravity-powered generation. Applicable construction, environmental, electrical-safety and other regulatory requirements must also be verified.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Burundi and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively by the owner for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements.

Burundi's electricity sector is governed principally by Law No. 1/13 of 23 April 2015 on the reorganisation of the electricity sector.

The legislation opened electricity generation to private operators, subject to the applicable administrative regime.

A completely isolated self-consumption installation must therefore be assessed according to its installed capacity, technology and actual use of the electricity, together with applicable environmental, construction, land-use and safety requirements.

Technology Gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation system
Operating Mode Completely off-grid / isolated / island operation

Electricity Import No

Operating Configuration Independent electrical island with no physical connection to the public electricity network
Main Electricity Law Law No. 1/13 of 23 April 2015 on the reorganisation of the electricity sector
Administrative Requirements

Burundi distinguishes electricity-generation installations according to their capacity.

  • Generation systems below 500 kW are subject to declaration.
  • Generation systems above 500 kW require authorisation.
  • Hydroelectric projects above 1 MW are subject to a concession regime.
  • Projects located on State-owned land can also require a public-private partnership arrangement.

These thresholds concern electricity-generation regulation generally and should not automatically be interpreted as a special exemption for every gravity-powered installation.

The project should therefore be classified according to its actual technology and installed electrical capacity before construction.

Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • Maintain complete physical separation from the public electricity network.
  • Do not import electricity from the public grid.
  • Do not export or sell electricity to third parties.
  • Use the electricity exclusively on the same private site.
  • Document the installed electrical capacity.
  • Determine whether the project exceeds the 500 kW authorisation threshold.
  • Determine whether the installation constitutes a hydroelectric project exceeding 1 MW.
  • Verify environmental, construction, land-use and safety requirements before construction.
Maximum Electrical Power
Confirmed regulatory threshold:

500 kW is the relevant threshold identified for the distinction between declaration and authorisation for electricity-generation systems.

Under the electricity-sector framework, generation systems below 500 kW are subject to declaration, whereas systems above 500 kW require authorisation.

For hydroelectric projects, installations above 1 MW are subject to a concession regime.

Therefore, 500 kW should be used as the principal regulatory capacity threshold for a non-hydroelectric gravity-powered self-generation project, rather than presenting it as a maximum technically exploitable power.

References
  1. Law No. 1/13 of 23 April 2015 on the Reorganisation of the Electricity Sector.
  2. Article 24 concerning self-generation and administrative authorisation/declaration.
  3. Article 38 concerning electricity installations exceeding 1 MW and the concession/PPP regime.
  4. Decree No. 100/130 of 23 June 2016 concerning electricity transmission, distribution and commercialisation.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The 500 kW and 1 MW figures identify regulatory thresholds found in the applicable electricity framework; they do not constitute a statement that a gravity-powered installation can technically produce that amount of electricity. The actual permissible project capacity must be verified with the competent Burundian authorities according to the technology, site, capacity and operating configuration.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Cabo Verde and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The installation is intended to operate independently from the public electricity network, with no electricity import, export or sale to third parties.

Cabo Verde regulates electricity generation through its electricity-sector legislation and licensing framework, including specific provisions for independent producers and self-producers.

Decreto-Lei No. 30/2006 established procedures for licensing independent producers and self-producers, while Decreto-Lei No. 1/2011 established a framework for independent and self-production from renewable energy sources.

A purely isolated installation must nevertheless be assessed with the competent energy authorities because the absence of a grid connection does not by itself establish a universal capacity exemption.

Administrative Requirements

Cabo Verde maintains a licensing framework for electricity production, including independent production and self-production.

  • Decreto-Lei No. 30/2006 establishes procedures for licensing independent producers and self-producers.
  • Decreto-Lei No. 1/2011 regulates the promotion, licensing and operation of independent production and self-production from renewable energy sources.
  • The general electricity regime requires the applicable production activity to be licensed by the competent energy authority.
  • Construction, environmental and technical requirements may apply independently.

No reliable nationwide capacity exemption specific to a gravity-powered, completely isolated installation was identified in the sources reviewed.

Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • Maintain complete physical isolation from the public electricity network.
  • Do not import electricity from the grid.
  • Do not export or sell electricity.
  • Keep generation and consumption on the same private site.
  • Obtain a written classification from the competent energy authority before construction.
  • Document the installed electrical capacity and technology.
  • Verify environmental, construction and safety requirements.
Maximum Electrical Power
Exact nationwide exemption threshold: Not identified in the authoritative sources reviewed for a completely off-grid gravity-powered self-consumption facility.

Cabo Verde has a licensing framework for self-production and independent production.

The available legislation confirms that self-production is a regulated activity, but the sources reviewed do not establish a single gravity-specific maximum electrical power below which the installation is automatically exempt.

The website should therefore not insert an invented kW figure. The project capacity should be submitted to the competent authority for confirmation before construction.

  2. Decreto-Lei No. 1/2011 — promotion, licensing and operation of renewable independent production and self-production.
  3. Cabo Verde electricity-sector regulatory framework.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. No gravity-specific capacity exemption has been inserted where an authoritative source did not establish one. The competent Cabo Verde energy authority should confirm the applicable licensing regime for the proposed technology, capacity and isolated operating configuration.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Cameroon and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The facility is intended to operate completely independently from the public electricity network.

Cameroon expressly regulates self-generation installations according to their installed capacity.

The official MINEE user guide identifies three relevant regimes for self-generation: freedom, declaration and authorisation.

This makes Cameroon one of the countries in this group for which a precise capacity classification can be established from the available regulatory documentation.

Technical Information
Country Cameroon 🇨🇲
Technology Gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation system
Operating Mode Completely off-grid / isolated
Public Grid Connection None intended
Electricity Import No
Electricity Export No
Electricity Sale No
Electricity Purchase No
Purpose Internal self-consumption
Grid Injection No
Operating Configuration Independent electrical island with no physical connection to the public grid
Administrative Requirements

The official MINEE documentation establishes the following self-generation thresholds.

  • Up to and including 100 kW: self-generation installations other than hydroelectric plants are not subject to legal or administrative formalities, provided they comply with approved standards and safety requirements.
  • More than 100 kW and less than 1 MW: prior declaration to the Electricity Sector Regulatory Agency is required.
  • More than 1 MW: the installation falls under the authorisation regime.

The documentation specifically excludes hydroelectric installations from the ≤100 kW administrative-freedom provision. A gravity-powered system using no hydroelectric resource should therefore be technically classified accordingly.

Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • Keep the installation physically isolated from the public network.
  • Do not import electricity.
  • Do not export or sell electricity.
  • For a non-hydroelectric installation, keep the capacity at or below 100 kW if the objective is to remain within the documented freedom regime.
  • If capacity exceeds 100 kW and remains below 1 MW, complete the required declaration.
  • If capacity exceeds 1 MW, obtain the applicable authorisation before commissioning.
  • Verify construction, environmental and safety requirements independently.
Maximum Electrical Power
Maximum capacity identified for the administrative freedom regime:

100 kW

For self-generation installations other than hydroelectric plants, the MINEE guide states that installations with a capacity of 100 kW or less are not subject to legal or administrative formalities, provided they comply with approved standards and safety norms.

Above 100 kW and below 1 MW, a declaration is required.

Above 1 MW, an authorisation is required.

Accordingly, 100 kW is the precise capacity threshold to use on this website for a non-hydroelectric gravity-powered self-consumption installation seeking to remain within the documented freedom regime.

References
  1. Ministry of Water Resources and Energy (MINEE), Guide Usager 2022.
  2. Cameroonian electricity-sector legislation concerning self-generation.
  3. Electricity Sector Regulatory Agency declaration requirements.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The 100 kW threshold applies to the regulatory category identified by the Cameroonian MINEE documentation for self-generation installations other than hydroelectric plants. The actual technical output of a gravity-powered installation depends on its mechanical and electrical design.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in the Union of the Comoros and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The Comorian electricity framework has recently been supplemented by Decree No. 26-070/PR of 4 June 2026, concerning renewable-energy self-production and the organisation of electricity mini-grids.

The new framework addresses individual and collective renewable-energy self-production, renewable-energy self-production communities and mini-grids.

It also establishes a framework for possible injection of surplus electricity into the national network.

A completely isolated installation that neither imports nor exports electricity must nevertheless be assessed according to the detailed implementing provisions.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Electricity-sector activities in the DRC are governed principally by the legislation relating to the electricity sector, including the 2014 electricity law and subsequent amendments and implementing provisions.

The DRC expressly recognizes the concept of an auto-producer, meaning a person or entity producing electricity for its own consumption.

The legal regime applicable to private self-production depends in particular on the installed capacity and whether the installation is established outside the public domain.

A completely isolated self-consumption installation must therefore be assessed according to the applicable capacity regime while also complying with technical, environmental, construction and safety requirements.

Technical Information
Country Democratic Republic of the Congo 🇨🇩
Technology Gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation / gravity energy storage system
Operating Mode Completely off-grid / isolated / island operation
Public Grid Connection None intended
Electricity Import No
Electricity Export No
Electricity Sale No
Electricity Purchase No
Purpose Internal household, industrial and corporate self-consumption
Electricity Market Participation No
Distribution to Third Parties No
Supply to Third Parties No
Grid Injection No
Grid Import No
Operating Configuration Independent electrical island with no physical connection to the public electricity network
Auto-production Definition Electricity production for the producer's own consumption
Electricity-Sector Framework DRC electricity-sector legislation, including the 2014 Electricity Law and subsequent amendments
Administrative Requirements

The DRC does not treat every private electricity installation in the same manner. The applicable administrative regime depends principally on the installed capacity and the legal characteristics of the installation.

Capacity Regimes for Private Self-production

For an auto-producer operating outside the public domain, the legislation establishes several capacity categories.

  • Below 50 kW: private electricity-generating installations fall under the freedom regime, subject to the applicable technical and safety requirements.
  • 51–99 kW: an auto-producer must submit a written declaration to the local administration responsible for electricity.
  • 100–999.99 kW: an auto-production installation outside the public domain is subject to an authorization regime.
  • 1 MW and above: independent electricity production is generally subject to the licensing regime, depending on the precise legal classification and purpose of the facility.
Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Electricity-sector authorization or declaration where applicable.
  • Technical certification and compliance requirements.
  • Construction and building requirements.
  • Land-use and planning requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Additional requirements associated with the particular technology and site.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, we recommend that:

  • The installation has no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for the producer's own requirements.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to the public grid.
  • The installed capacity is clearly documented.
  • The applicable DRC capacity regime is verified before construction.
  • Construction, environmental, planning and technical requirements are independently verified.
Maximum Electrical Power
DRC self-production threshold without electricity-sector authorization:

Below 50 kW for a private electricity-generating installation established outside the public domain, under the freedom regime identified in the electricity-sector legislation.

Installations from 51 kW to 99 kW fall under a declaration regime, while installations from 100 kW to 999.99 kW fall under an authorization regime.

Consequently, for a purely off-grid self-consumption installation intended to remain within the freedom regime, the relevant maximum capacity is less than 50 kW.

Demonstrated Gravity-Technology Benchmark

The largest commercial-scale gravity-energy storage installation identified in operation is the Rudong EVx system in China.

Its rated power is 25 MW with an energy capacity of 100 MWh.

This 25 MW figure is a demonstrated technology benchmark and is not a DRC electricity-law exemption threshold.

Website classification for the DRC:

Legal self-consumption freedom regime: < 50 kW

Declaration regime: 51–99 kW

Authorization regime: 100–999.99 kW

Demonstrated gravity technology: 25 MW / 100 MWh
References
  1. Loi n°14/011 du 17 juin 2014 relative au secteur de l'électricité — principal DRC electricity-sector framework.
  2. DRC Electricity Law — Articles 74–77 — authorization, declaration and freedom regimes for electricity installations.
  3. DRC electricity-sector implementing framework — capacity-based administrative regimes.
  4. ARE — Annual Report 2024 — confirmation of the current capacity classification for self-production.
  5. Energy Vault — Rudong EVx — 25 MW / 100 MWh commercial gravity-energy storage benchmark.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The applicable DRC requirements should be verified with the competent provincial, local and electricity-sector authorities before developing, constructing or operating a gravity-powered electricity-generation facility. Requirements may depend on installed capacity, ownership of the land, location, technology, environmental characteristics, construction, safety requirements and the actual use of the electricity.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in the Republic of the Congo and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate requirements under the control of the producer.

The principal electricity-sector framework is the Law No. 14-2003 of 10 April 2003 establishing the Electricity Code .

The Electricity Code expressly defines an auto-producer as a person or entity producing electricity for personal purposes.

Article 40 establishes that the right of an auto-producer to operate depends on installed capacity and may be subject to a freedom, declaration or authorization regime.

The exact thresholds for these regimes are to be specified by implementing regulation. A specific nationwide kW exemption threshold should therefore not be invented where the applicable official threshold has not been identified.

Electricity Market Participation No

Supply to Third Parties No

Grid Import No
Operating Configuration Independent electrical island with no physical connection to the public electricity network
National Electricity Framework Law No. 14-2003 of 10 April 2003 establishing the Electricity Code
Administrative Requirements

The Electricity Code does not make self-production automatically exempt from administrative regulation.

Auto-production Regime

Article 40 provides that the right of an auto-producer to operate is determined according to installed capacity.

Depending on capacity, the activity may be subject to:

  • a freedom regime;
  • a prior administrative declaration; or
  • an administrative authorization.

Article 41 provides that the applicable regimes, conditions and thresholds are to be specified by regulatory provisions.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Electricity-sector declaration or authorization where applicable.
  • Certificate of conformity.
  • Construction requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Land-use and planning requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Additional requirements arising from the particular technology and site.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain genuinely isolated and dedicated to self-consumption, we recommend that:

  • No physical connection is made to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported.
  • No electricity is exported.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • Electricity is consumed exclusively by the producer.
  • The installation is operated in electrical island mode.
  • Appropriate electrical protection prevents accidental grid energisation.
  • The installed capacity is documented precisely.
  • The applicable implementing regulations are checked before construction.
  • A certificate of conformity is obtained where required.
Maximum Electrical Power
Republic of the Congo legal threshold:

The Electricity Code establishes capacity-based freedom, declaration and authorization regimes for auto-producers, but Article 41 delegates the precise thresholds to implementing regulations.

No reliable official nationwide kW exemption threshold has been identified in the sources reviewed.

It would therefore be incorrect to insert a fabricated kW figure as the maximum legally exempt capacity.

Demonstrated Gravity-Technology Benchmark

The Rudong EVx gravity-energy-storage facility in China has a rated electrical output of 25 MW and an energy capacity of 100 MWh.

It represents a demonstrated commercial-scale gravity technology benchmark and does not constitute a Republic of the Congo legal threshold.

Website classification for the Republic of the Congo:

Legal capacity threshold: to be determined from the applicable implementing regulations.

Demonstrated gravity technology: 25 MW / 100 MWh

  2. Article 40 — capacity-dependent regimes applicable to electricity auto-producers.
  3. Article 41 — implementing regulation for the regimes and conditions applicable to auto-producers.
  4. Article 69 — certificate of conformity for electricity production, transport and distribution installations.
  5. Energy Vault — Rudong EVx — 25 MW / 100 MWh commercial gravity-energy storage benchmark.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The applicable Republic of the Congo electricity, construction, environmental, land-use and safety requirements should be verified with the competent authorities before developing, constructing or operating a gravity-powered electricity-generation facility. In particular, the precise capacity thresholds applicable to auto-production should be verified against the implementing regulations in force at the time of the project.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Côte d'Ivoire and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Côte d'Ivoire's electricity sector is principally governed by Law No. 2014-132 of 24 March 2014 establishing the Electricity Code.

The Electricity Code expressly recognizes "autoproduction" as electricity production principally intended for the producer's own consumption.

Article 8 establishes freedom, declaration and authorization regimes according to installed capacity.

The Directorate-General for Energy specifies the applicable self-production thresholds, including different thresholds for conventional energy and new and renewable energy.

Administrative Requirements

Côte d'Ivoire expressly regulates electricity self-production according to installed capacity.

Self-production Capacity Thresholds

According to the Directorate-General for Energy, prior authorization is required for cumulative installed self-production capacity above:

  • 20 kW for conventional-energy self-production.
  • 400 kW for new and renewable-energy self-production.

The classification of a particular gravity system should therefore be confirmed before relying on the 400 kW renewable-energy threshold.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Prior declaration or authorization, depending on installed capacity and energy classification.
  • Technical compliance requirements.
  • Construction and planning requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Site-specific requirements.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, we recommend that:

  • The installation has no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • Electricity is consumed exclusively by the producer.
  • The system operates in island mode.
  • Appropriate electrical protection prevents accidental grid connection.
  • The installed capacity is documented precisely.
  • The technology is legally classified before selecting the applicable capacity threshold.
Maximum Electrical Power
Relevant renewable self-production threshold:

400 kW is the threshold identified by the Directorate-General for Energy above which prior authorization applies to self-production based on new and renewable energy.

This threshold should not be treated as a universal technical limit for gravity technology.

The Electricity Code defines new and renewable energy and specifically addresses hydraulic energy with a distinction at 10 MW.

The legal classification of a gravity-powered system should therefore be confirmed with the competent Ivorian energy authority before applying the 400 kW threshold.

Demonstrated Gravity-Technology Benchmark

The Rudong EVx gravity-energy-storage facility in China has demonstrated a peak electrical output of 25 MW and an energy capacity of 100 MWh.

This 25 MW value is a technology benchmark, not an Ivorian legal exemption threshold.

Website classification for Côte d'Ivoire:

Renewable self-production authorization threshold: > 400 kW

Conventional-energy self-production authorization threshold: > 20 kW

Demonstrated gravity technology: 25 MW / 100 MWh

  2. Article 1 — definition of electricity self-production.
  3. Article 8 — freedom, declaration and authorization regimes based on installed capacity.
  4. Directorate-General for Energy — Côte d'Ivoire — self-production authorization thresholds: 20 kW conventional and 400 kW new and renewable.
  5. Energy Vault — Rudong EVx — 25 MW / 100 MWh gravity-energy-storage technology benchmark.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The applicable Ivorian electricity, environmental, construction, planning and safety requirements should be verified before developing, constructing or operating a gravity-powered electricity-generation facility. In particular, the legal classification of the gravity technology as a new or renewable energy source should be confirmed before relying on the 400 kW threshold.

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Egypt and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Egypt's principal electricity-sector legislation is Electricity Law No. 87 of 2015 and its Executive Regulations issued by Decree No. 230 of 2016.

Article 13 of Electricity Law No. 87 of 2015 requires a licence for electricity production activities in principle.

However, the law expressly provides that electricity producers generating electricity for their own use may be exempted from permits and licences, subject to conditions established by the Executive Regulations.

The specific regulatory treatment therefore depends on the type of installation, its capacity, whether it is connected to the grid and whether it falls under specific renewable-energy self-consumption rules.

Egypt applies a licensing framework to electricity production, but the Electricity Law specifically provides for possible exemptions for producers generating electricity for their own use.

Self-consumption Treatment

Article 13 of Electricity Law No. 87 of 2015 provides that electricity producers for their own use may be exempted from permits and licences.

The detailed conditions are established through the Executive Regulations and subsequent regulatory instruments.

The specific rules identified for solar self-consumption should not automatically be extended to a gravity-powered installation without confirmation from EgyptERA.

Egypt-wide maximum for an off-grid gravity self-consumption installation:

No single technology-neutral maximum kW/MW threshold has been identified in the reviewed Egyptian legislation for a completely isolated gravity-powered self-consumption installation.

Electricity Law No. 87 of 2015 provides a possible exemption for electricity producers generating electricity for their own use, but the detailed conditions are established by the Executive Regulations.

EgyptERA Circular No. 3 of 2023 specifically addresses solar photovoltaic self-consumption and includes regulatory provisions for isolated/off-grid installations. It should not be treated as a universal capacity limit for gravity technology.

Overview

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Electricity-sector activities in Equatorial Guinea are subject to State regulation. Electricity supply services are identified as public-sector reserved services, while the State may delegate, grant concessions or associate with private initiatives under the conditions established by law.

Publicly available official material confirms that Equatorial Guinea has been developing and reforming its electricity-sector legislation, including a proposed regulatory framework for the electricity sector and renewable-energy implementing regulations.

Because a current, authoritative capacity exemption specifically applicable to a completely isolated self-consumption generation installation could not be verified, the project should not be assumed to be exempt solely because it is off-grid.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Eswatini and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is completely isolated from the public electricity network and does not import or export electricity.

Eswatini's electricity sector is regulated principally under the Electricity Act, 2007 and by the Eswatini Energy Regulatory Authority (ESERA).

The legislation expressly regulates electricity generation and off-grid and mini-grid electricity supplies.

Importantly for an own-use project, ESERA states that electricity generators for own use are exempt from holding a generation licence, but a generator with a facility capacity of 100 kW or above must apply for an exemption.

Administrative Requirements

ESERA confirms that electricity generation is a regulated power-system activity.

However, generators producing electricity for their own use are exempted from the obligation to hold a generation licence.

ESERA further states that where the generation capacity is 100 kW or above, the own-use generator must apply for an exemption.

Own-Use Generation

The relevant regulatory distinction is therefore not simply whether the system is off-grid. The own-use status and installed generation capacity must be considered.

A facility below 100 kW should nevertheless be checked against the current ESERA licensing rules, technical requirements and other applicable legislation before construction.

Other Potential Requirements
  • ESERA exemption application for own-use generation at or above 100 kW.
  • Construction approval.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Land-use requirements.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Fire and occupational safety requirements.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • Keep the facility physically isolated from the public electricity network.
  • Use electricity exclusively for own consumption.
  • Do not sell electricity to third parties.
  • Do not import electricity from the public grid.
  • Do not export electricity to the public grid.
  • Apply to ESERA for the applicable exemption when the facility is 100 kW or above.
  • Maintain electrical protection preventing accidental grid energisation.
Maximum Electrical Power
Eswatini own-use threshold: 100 kW is the threshold at which an own-use generator must apply for an exemption from the generation-licence obligation.

This should not be interpreted as a maximum permitted generation capacity. It is an exemption-application threshold.

Facilities of 100 kW or more can therefore be operated for own use subject to obtaining the applicable exemption and satisfying the regulatory requirements.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Gabon and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is completely isolated from the public electricity network, without electricity imports or exports.

Gabon's electricity legislation expressly regulates self-generation (autoproduction) installations.

Law No. 2016-012 of 2023 establishes different regulatory regimes according to the installed power of self-generation installations.

The legislation provides a declaration regime for self-generation installations above 100 kW and below 1 MW and an authorization regime for installations above 1 MW.

Administrative Requirements

Gabon's electricity legislation provides a specific regulatory structure for self-generation facilities.

Self-generation above 100 kW and below 1 MW

Article 71 provides that where the power of a self-generation installation is greater than 100 kW and less than 1 MW, the owner must make a prior declaration before commissioning to the Ministry responsible for Energy.

Self-generation above 1 MW

Article 69 establishes an authorization regime for self-generation installations with a power greater than 1 MW.

Article 70 further specifies the conditions under which this authorization may be granted.

  • Water authorization where applicable.

  • Use the electricity exclusively for internal self-consumption.
  • Do not export electricity.
  • Do not import electricity.
  • Determine the exact installed generation power before selecting the legal procedure.
  • Submit the required declaration when the facility is above 100 kW and below 1 MW.
  • Obtain the applicable authorization when the facility exceeds 1 MW.
  • Prevent accidental connection to the public grid.
Maximum Electrical Power
Gabon self-generation threshold: 100 kW is the upper boundary below which the specific Article 71 declaration regime is not triggered by the stated >100 kW threshold.

Above 100 kW and below 1 MW, a prior declaration is required.

Above 1 MW, the installation falls under the authorization regime established by Article 69.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in The Gambia and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Electricity generation in The Gambia is regulated principally under the Electricity Act 2005, together with the regulatory framework administered by the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA).

The Electricity Act 2005 generally requires a licence for electricity generation, transmission, dispatch or distribution.

However, the Act expressly provides that a licence is not required for electricity generation solely for consumption at the site of the generating facility.

Consequently, a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation must be assessed under the specific site-generation exemption, while remaining subject to applicable construction, environmental, electrical safety and other legal requirements.

Administrative Requirements

The Electricity Act 2005 establishes a general licensing requirement for electricity generation.

However, section 5(2)(a) expressly provides that a licence is not required for electricity generation solely for consumption at the site of the generating facility.

On-site Self-consumption Exemption

The Electricity Act 2005 provides an exemption from the electricity-generation licensing requirement where electricity is generated solely for consumption at the site of the generating facility.

The exemption is therefore particularly relevant to a genuinely isolated self-consumption facility.

The legislation reviewed does not provide a numerical kW/MW ceiling in section 5(2)(a) for this specific site-consumption exemption.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Verification of the Electricity Act self-consumption exemption.
  • PURA regulatory requirements where applicable.
  • Construction and building requirements.
  • Land-use and planning requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Water-law authorization where water resources are used.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Technology-specific safety requirements.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, we recommend that:

  • The installation has no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • Electricity is consumed exclusively at the site of the generating facility.
  • No electricity is supplied to external customers.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to the public grid.
  • The installation is documented as an on-site self-consumption facility.
  • The Electricity Act 2005 exemption is verified with the competent authority before construction.
  • Construction, environmental, planning and electrical safety requirements are independently verified.
Maximum Electrical Power
Verified numerical maximum for the specific self-consumption exemption:

No numerical kW/MW maximum was identified in section 5(2)(a) of the Electricity Act 2005 for electricity generation solely for consumption at the generating site.

The Electricity Act 2005 establishes a general generation-licensing requirement but expressly excludes electricity generation solely for consumption at the generating site from that requirement.

The legal text reviewed does not attach a specific installed-capacity figure to this exemption.

Therefore, it would be incorrect to insert an arbitrary value such as 100 kW, 500 kW or 1 MW as the legal maximum for this specific exemption.

Website classification for The Gambia:

No numerical capacity ceiling identified in the specific statutory site-consumption exemption.

The exemption must nevertheless be confirmed against the complete regulatory framework and the actual configuration of the proposed facility.

The maximum electrical capacity for the proposed gravity-powered facility should therefore be determined after written confirmation from the competent Gambian electricity authority rather than by assuming a numerical threshold that is not stated in the reviewed legislation.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Ghana regulates electricity generation through the Energy Commission and the national electricity regulatory framework.

The Renewable Energy Act 2011 and the Energy Commission's regulatory framework are particularly relevant where the technology is classified as a renewable-energy electricity-generation technology.

Administrative Requirements

Ghana's electricity regulatory framework distinguishes electricity generation, mini-grid operation and grid-connected renewable self-generation.

Important distinction concerning the 100 kW threshold

Ghanaian mini-grid rules use a 100 kW threshold in the regulatory treatment of mini-grids.

Mini-grids exceeding 100 kW and up to 1 MW have been subject to licensing requirements, while smaller mini-grids have been subject to registration requirements.

These mini-grid thresholds must not be treated as a general nationwide exemption for a completely isolated private self-consumption electricity-generation facility.

Grid-connected Renewable Generation

Ghana also operates a net-metering framework for renewable-energy generating systems connected to the distribution network.

That framework is not the appropriate classification for a facility that has no physical connection to the public electricity network and does not export electricity.

Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, we recommend that:

  • The facility has no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • Electricity is consumed exclusively by the operator or owner.
  • The facility is not operated as a mini-grid supplying external consumers.
  • No electricity trading is undertaken.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to the public network.
  • The facility is documented as an isolated self-consumption installation.
  • The Energy Commission classification is confirmed before construction.
Maximum Electrical Power
Verified maximum specifically applicable to private isolated self-consumption:

No separate numerical nationwide capacity ceiling for a completely isolated private self-consumption facility has been verified from the sources reviewed.

Ghanaian regulations contain numerical thresholds for particular electricity-sector configurations, including mini-grids.

The 100 kW and 1 MW thresholds associated with mini-grid regulation should not be presented as a general maximum for every off-grid electricity generator.

Mini-grid thresholds — not applicable automatically to private self-consumption

Mini-grid regulatory material identifies installations up to 100 kW for registration and larger installations up to 1 MW for licensing.

Those values concern mini-grid operation and should not be entered as the maximum capacity of the proposed isolated gravity-powered self-consumption facility.

Website classification for Ghana:

No verified national numerical maximum identified specifically for a completely isolated private self-consumption facility.

The 100 kW / 1 MW mini-grid thresholds must not be substituted for an off-grid self-consumption limit.

The exact permissible capacity should therefore be confirmed with the Energy Commission of Ghana based on the technology, installed capacity, location, ownership and actual operating configuration.

References
  1. Renewable Energy Act 2011, Act 832 — principal renewable-energy legislative framework.
  2. Energy Commission of Ghana — electricity and renewable-energy regulatory authority.
  3. Energy Commission Net Metering Code 2023 — grid-connected renewable self-generation framework.
  4. Ghana Mini-grid regulatory framework — regulatory thresholds concerning mini-grid installations.
  5. Applicable construction, environmental, planning, electrical and safety requirements.
Public Information Notice

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The numerical thresholds applicable to Ghanaian mini-grids should not be interpreted as a general capacity limit for an isolated private self-consumption facility. The proposed gravity-powered electricity-generation project should be classified by the competent Ghanaian authority according to its technology, capacity, location, operating configuration and whether electricity is supplied to third parties.

Overview

We are considering a gravity-powered low-carbon electricity generation facility located in Kenya and operated exclusively for internal self-consumption.

The intended installation is designed to operate independently from the public electricity network, without importing electricity from or exporting electricity to the public electricity grid.

Electricity would be used exclusively for internal household, industrial or corporate electricity requirements under the control of the producer.

Kenya regulates electricity generation under the Energy Act 2019 and the electricity licensing regulations administered by the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA).

The current licensing framework contains an explicit exemption for persons generating electricity for their own use where the capacity does not exceed 1 MW.

Administrative Requirements

Kenya's 2024 electricity licensing regulations expressly exclude persons generating electricity for their own use where the capacity does not exceed 1 MW.

Own-use Generation Exemption

The Energy (Electric Power Undertaking Licensing) Regulations, 2024 provide that the licensing regulations do not apply to a person generating electrical energy for their own use where the capacity does not exceed 1 MW.

This is the principal numerical threshold relevant to the proposed private self-consumption configuration.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • EPRA requirements where applicable.
  • Construction and building approvals.
  • Environmental approvals.
  • Land-use and planning requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Water authorization where applicable.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk
  • Installed generation capacity should not exceed 1 MW where relying on the own-use licensing exemption.
  • The installation should have no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity should be imported from the grid.
  • No electricity should be exported to the grid.
  • No electricity should be sold to third parties.
  • Electricity should be used exclusively for internal consumption.
  • Electrical protection should prevent accidental grid connection.
  • The installation should be documented as captive / own-use generation.
  • The 1 MW threshold should be verified against the final installed electrical configuration.
Maximum Electrical Power
Kenya maximum capacity for the own-use licensing exemption:

1 MW

The Energy (Electric Power Undertaking Licensing) Regulations, 2024 expressly exclude electricity generated for the generator's own use where the capacity does not exceed 1 MW.

The Kenyan Ministry of Energy also identifies 1 MW as the threshold above which a generation licence is required for captive power.

Website classification for Kenya:

Maximum capacity under the own-use licensing exemption: 1 MW.

A facility above this threshold should be assessed for the applicable generation licence and other regulatory approvals.

The 1 MW value is a regulatory licensing threshold for own-use generation; it is not a statement that every gravity-powered installation can technically produce that amount of electricity.

Other approvals, including environmental, construction, land-use, electrical safety and technology-specific requirements, may remain applicable.
