Administrative Requirements

An isolated electricity-generation installation should not be considered automatically exempt from administrative requirements merely because it does not exchange electricity with the public grid.

Vatican City State has a distinct sovereign legal and administrative system. Electricity-generation projects are therefore to be assessed under the applicable Vatican authorities and instruments rather than automatically applying the electricity-generation licensing thresholds of Italy.

Vatican City State Electricity Framework

The Vatican City State administers its own infrastructure and public services through the Governorate of Vatican City State.

The Governorate's Directorate for Infrastructure and Services is responsible for infrastructure, electrical systems and related technical activities within the State.

Official Vatican sources confirm that the Governorate is actively developing renewable electricity-generation systems as part of its energy-efficiency and environmental programme.

The available public sources do not identify a general Vatican-wide electricity-generation exemption expressed as a fixed kW threshold specifically for an isolated gravity-powered electricity-generation installation.

Renewable Electricity Development

Vatican City State has already implemented photovoltaic electricity-generation systems.

The Governorate reported that two photovoltaic systems associated with the Vatican Museums and the Vignaccia warehouse were expected to provide a combined photovoltaic peak power of 350 kWp .

The same official source reported an expected combined electricity production of approximately 500 MWh per year .

This 350 kWp figure is an officially documented installed/reference generation capacity. It is not identified by the Vatican sources as a legal maximum capacity for all electricity-generation technologies.

Other Potential Administrative Requirements
  • Authorization or approval by the competent Vatican authority where required.
  • Construction and building requirements.
  • Structural engineering requirements.
  • Electrical safety requirements.
  • Fire-safety requirements.
  • Occupational health and safety requirements.
  • Environmental requirements.
  • Land-use and site-specific requirements.
  • Requirements applicable to mechanical and electrical machinery.
  • Additional technical requirements arising from the specific gravity-generation technology.
  • Additional requirements applicable to installations located in or affecting protected cultural or historical areas.
Measures to Reduce Licensing Risk

For a project intended to remain a genuinely isolated self-consumption installation, we recommend that:

  • The electricity-generation installation has no physical connection to the public electricity network.
  • No electricity is imported from the public grid.
  • No electricity is exported to the public grid.
  • No electricity is sold to third parties.
  • No electricity is purchased from the public grid for operation of the isolated system.
  • No electricity trading is undertaken.
  • No participation in electricity balancing or aggregation markets is undertaken.
  • Electricity is used exclusively for internal self-consumption under the control of the producer.
  • The installation operates independently in island mode.
  • Electrical protection prevents accidental connection to or energisation of an external electricity network.
  • The installation is documented as a private or institutional self-consumption facility.
  • The competent Vatican authority is consulted before construction.
  • The mechanical, structural and electrical safety of the gravity-generation system is independently verified.
  • Construction, fire-safety, environmental and heritage requirements are independently verified.
Maximum Electrical Power
Documented Vatican renewable-generation capacity:

350 kWp

The Governorate of Vatican City State officially reported a combined photovoltaic peak capacity of approximately 350 kWp for two photovoltaic systems associated with the Vatican Museums and the Vignaccia warehouse.

The official Vatican source identifies the combined capacity of the two photovoltaic systems as 350 kWp and their expected combined annual electricity production as approximately 500 MWh/year .

The photovoltaic system installed at the Cortile delle Corazze at the entrance to the Vatican Museums has a nominal power output of approximately 135 kWp and an expected annual production of approximately 164 MWh/year .

Reference Capacity for the Project

For the purposes of this comparative project database, the relevant documented Vatican renewable-generation reference capacity is:

350 kWp

This figure corresponds to an officially documented renewable electricity-generation installation in Vatican City State.

It should not be described as a statutory exemption threshold for a gravity-powered installation. No publicly identified Vatican provision establishes 350 kW as a technology- specific legal ceiling for gravity-powered electricity generation.

Application to Gravity-Powered Generation

The proposed technology is a gravity-powered electricity-generation system rather than a photovoltaic system.

Consequently, the photovoltaic capacity of 350 kWp cannot automatically be treated as a technology-specific legal limit for gravity generation.

The project should therefore be submitted to the competent Vatican authority with the exact installed electrical capacity, mechanical configuration, operating mode, protection system and site characteristics.

Until a specific Vatican authorization or regulation establishes another capacity threshold, the safest factual classification is to use 350 kWp as the documented Vatican renewable-generation reference capacity rather than presenting it as a statutory exemption.

Website classification for Vatican City:

Documented renewable-generation reference: 350 kWp

The Vatican City State has officially documented renewable electricity-generation installations with a combined peak capacity of approximately 350 kWp.

Important: This is a documented generation capacity and not a statutory maximum specifically established for gravity-powered electricity-generation installations.

For the comparative table, the recommended value is therefore 350 kWp, classified as "documented renewable-generation reference capacity" rather than as an electricity-law exemption threshold.

This information is provided for general public information purposes only. The figure of 350 kWp is based on an officially documented renewable electricity-generation installation in Vatican City State and should not be interpreted as a statutory exemption threshold specifically applicable to gravity-powered electricity generation. Before developing, constructing or operating a gravity-powered electricity-generation facility, the applicable Vatican authorities should be consulted concerning authorization, construction, electrical safety, mechanical safety, fire protection, environmental protection, heritage protection, land-use requirements and the specific installed electrical capacity of the proposed installation.

Fundamental Research – Chas Campbell Gravitational Engine

This section gathers the theoretical background and engineering notes used to study the mechanical behavior of the Chas Campbell gravitational engine concept.
The documentation focuses on classical mechanics, rotational dynamics, energy conservation, flywheel analysis, and transmission design.
It is intended as a research resource for understanding and modeling the proposed mechanism, rather than as experimental validation of over-unity or perpetual-motion operation.

  • Fundamental principles of rotational dynamics
  • Potential and kinetic energy of pendulum systems
  • Mechanical energy conservation
  • Flywheel dynamic modeling
  • Torque, power and transmission ratio calculations
  • Mathematical derivation of the motion equations
  • Motor, generator and pulley sizing methodology

The objective of this research is to provide a mathematical framework for numerical simulation and engineering analysis of the proposed mechanical architecture using established principles of Newtonian mechanics.


Course
Fundamental principle of rotating dynamics
We have :
\[ F_{t} = m * a_{t} \]
is the tangential component of the resultant forces.

We have :
\[ C = F_{t} * r \]
is the moment of force with respect to the origin in N*m.

We have :
\[ a_{t} = r * \frac{\mathrm d \omega}{\mathrm d t} \]

Gravitational energy of simple pendulum
We have :
\[ E_{p} = m * g * r * (1 - cos(\theta)) \]

Kinetic energy of simple pendulum
We have :
\[ E_{c} = 1/2 * m * V^{2} \]
\[ E_{c} = 1/2 * m * (\omega * r)^{2} \]

Energy conservation of simple pendulum
We have :
\[ E_{m} = E_{c} + E_{p} \]
is the mechanical energy of the system.

\[ E_{m} = \frac{1}{2} * m * (\omega * r)^{2} + m * g * r * (1 - cos(\theta)) \]

Engine torque
We have :
\[ P_{motor} = C_{motor} * \omega_{motor} \]

Pulley-belt ratio or drive ratio
We have :
\[ \frac{d_{out}}{d_{in}} = \frac{\omega_{in}}{\omega_{out}} = \frac{C_{out}}{C_{in}} \]

Proof
We have the schematic of the flywheel :

We have : \[ E_{c, flywheel} = M_{flywheel} * (\omega_{flywheel} * r_{flywheel})^{2} \] is the kinetic energy of the flywheel.

We have : \[ E_{p, flywheel} = 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * sin(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) \] is the potential energy of the flywheel.

We have : \[ E_{m,flywheel} = M_{flywheel} * (\omega_{flywheel} * r_{flywheel})^{2} + 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * sin(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) \] is the mechanical energy of the flywheel.

We have : \[ E_{m,flywheel} = M_{flywheel} * (\frac{\mathrm d \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t} * r_{flywheel})^{2} + 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * sin(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) \] \[ E_{m,flywheel} = M_{flywheel} * (\frac{\mathrm d \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t})^{2} * r_{flywheel}^{2} + 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * sin(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) \] \[ E_{m, flywheel} = constant \]

In derivating the mechanical energy of the flywheel, we have the moving equation of the flywheel : \[ \frac{\mathrm d E_{m, flywheel}}{\mathrm d t} = 0 \] \[ \frac{\mathrm d E_{m, flywheel}}{\mathrm d t} = 2 * M_{flywheel} * \frac{\mathrm d \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t} * \frac{\mathrm d^{2} \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t^{2}} * r_{flywheel}^{2} + 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * cos(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) \] \[ 2 * M_{flywheel} * \frac{\mathrm d \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t} * \frac{\mathrm d^{2} \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t^{2}} * r_{flywheel}^{2} + 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * \frac{\mathrm d \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t} * cos(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) = 0 \]
We have : \[ \frac{\mathrm d \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t} \ne 0 \] \[ \frac{\mathrm d^{2} \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t^{2}} + \frac{g}{r_{flywheel}} * cos(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) = 0 \] \[ \omega_{flywheel} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{r_{flywheel}}} \]
Parameters of the motor
Let be \[ \omega_{motor} = 1500 \] the angular speed in turns per minute.

Let be \[ C_{motor} = 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} \] the torque.

Let be \[ P_{m,motor} = C_{motor} * \omega_{motor} \] \[ P_{m,motor} = 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * \omega_{motor} \] the mechanical power.

Let be \[ P_{e,motor} = P_{m,motor} \] \[ P_{e,motor} = 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * \omega_{motor} \] the electrical power if there is no resistance.

Let be \[ d_{pulley,motor} \] the diameter of the pulley of the motor in meter.

Parameters of the electrical generator
Let be \[ \omega_{generator} = 60 * f_{generator} \] \[ \omega_{generator} = 60 * 50 \] \[ \omega_{generator} = 3000 \] the angular speed in turns per minute.

Let be \[ P_{e,generator} = E_{e,generator} * \omega_{generator} \] \[ E_{e,generator} = \frac{P_{e,generator}}{\omega_{generator}} \] the electrical power in watts.

Let be \[ E_{e,generator} = E_{m,flywheel} \] \[ M_{flywheel} * (\frac{\mathrm d \theta_{flywheel}(t)}{\mathrm d t})^{2} * r_{flywheel}^{2} + 2 * M_{flywheel} * g * r_{flywheel} * sin(\theta_{flywheel}(t)) = \frac{P_{e,generator}}{\omega_{generator}} \] the electrical energy in joules.

Let be \[ d_{pulley,generator} \] the diameter of the pulley of the generator in meter.

Parameters of the flywheel
Let be \[ \omega_{flywheel} = \frac{d_{pulley,motor} * \omega_{motor}}{d_{pulley,flywheel}} \] the angular speed in turns per minute.

Let be \[ d_{pulley,flywheel} = \frac{\omega_{generator} * d_{pulley,generator}}{\omega_{flywheel}} \] the diameter of all the pulleys of the flywheel in meter.

We have : \[ d_{pulley,generator} = \frac{\omega_{flywheel} * d_{pulley,flywheel}}{\omega_{generator}} \] \[ d_{pulley,motor} = \frac{\omega_{flywheel} * d_{pulley,flywheel}}{\omega_{motor}} \]

With \[ \theta_{flywheel}(t) = \frac{\pi}{2} \] , we have : \[ M_{flywheel} = \frac{P_{e,generator}}{\omega_{generator} * g * r_{flywheel} * 2} \]
